# Final independent MIDI review — 2026-10-20

**Verdict: review complete; request changes before unrestricted timing/conformance acceptance.** Final candidate `a33fc31f0e8b5ed46b48bfa435bf4629e36a1bf3`, remote `origin/task/midi-stream-lifecycle-oct20`. Final implementation receipt and DONE board entry inspected; fresh `ls-remote` agrees. Includes `7908e591` backpressure and final event-tag fix beyond `f0f203b`. Prior `bdb5bc86` review was incomplete and is not acceptance evidence.

## Concrete findings

1. **P1 timing: fractional tick durations disappear** — `lib/host-audio.js:2316`. Each event delay is independently floored before addition. At default tempo 500000 and supported division 960, 96 events with delta 1 should span 50 ms. Independent probe executes the actual WAT wrappers and host scheduler: restart/service at 100 ms plays all 96 notes and marks the buffer DONE at that same timestamp. This is not ordinary millisecond quantization: repeated truncation removes the entire duration. Preserve fractional accumulated time/remainder per stream, including tempo changes, pause/restart and stop/reset; add a nonintegral-delta regression. This defect is retained from the baseline integer-division scheduler, not newly introduced by the lifecycle patch. It blocks a general stream-timing correctness claim; coordinator must explicitly defer it if accepting only the narrower lifecycle improvement.

2. **P2 time-division state validation** — `lib/host-audio.js:3951`. Queue occupancy substitutes for stopped/running state. Independent probe restarts an empty stream and then SETs division 960: running=true, result=0, division changes. Microsoft permits setting time division only while stopped. Validate lifecycle state rather than queue length, with running-empty and stopped/queued cases. The baseline also lacked the running-state restriction; the candidate's new queue check does not repair it.

Normative sources: [MIDIEVENT](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/mmeapi/ns-mmeapi-midievent) defines delta time in ticks between events; [midiStreamProperty](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/mmeapi/nf-mmeapi-midistreamproperty) restricts time-division setting to stopped devices. Consulted primary Microsoft docs for [Stop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/mmeapi/nf-mmeapi-midistreamstop), [Reset](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/mmeapi/nf-mmeapi-midioutreset), and [Pause](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/mmeapi/nf-mmeapi-midistreampause) when checking lifecycle semantics.

## Verified scope

Independent immutable-tree replay: **22 behavioral groups PASS; 14 mutation controls killed**. Isolated module SHA-256 `373deb768589cd0bec8b6b990dc2d51cd63fbb5cafdb3a028475b6c8920617c5`. Implementation evidence verifier independently passes **15 artifact hashes and 25 source pins**, including final receipt, remote identity, and logged expected baseline negative. Existing wave regressions/generator/ESP gates are implementation-recorded results, not independently rerun here.

Source and assertions support independent live handles/synths/queues and callback registrations; invalid/closed/ordinary handles and foreign/pending header rejection; monotonic close/reopen handle identity; Stop versus Reset note/sustain behavior; detached queue draining and one completion per submission; reentrant DONE requeue/restart and close/reopen without rerouting old registrations. Public Stop hash lookup, generated dispatch and stdcall cleanup execute actual extracted production code. No additional defect was demonstrated in these bounded cases.

The final window change retains ordered OPEN/DONE/CLOSE records on failed queue insertion and retries via the completion pump. Its mutation removes the retry break and is killed. Event-tag rejection matches the real host SetEvent/ReleaseMutex discriminator; exact return value 1 is required. Unsupported thread/Worker function-window callbacks and unsupported event transports fail explicitly. Function callback admission uses actual browser owner/suspension/busy/wait bookkeeping and the production WAT saved frame.

## Test masks and remaining qualification

The harness replaces guest translation with identity memory, creates selected globals, traps unrelated dispatch branches, mocks synth/event/window transports, and simulates callback `ret 20` rather than executing guest x86. The window test substitutes `post_message_q`; it proves host retention/order, not native queue integration or wake/progress. Timing tests use integer-duration deltas and miss finding 1; property tests exercise stopped empty streams and miss finding 2. All 14 mutations require behavioral AssertionError, but none mutates fractional accumulation or running-state property checks. The two added probes modify only the test program in RAM; production blobs are unchanged.

Remaining required qualification: canonical integrated build and full VM/public x86 callback fixture; real guest translation and callback return/continuation; actual queue-full drain/retry, wait/suspension and cross-thread ownership; TinySynth/oscillator audio and resource lifetime. Scheduling still depends on timeGetTime service calls. Worker function/window callback transport, SysEx/long/position events and SMPTE remain unsupported. No source test qualifies original MadBomber gameplay, SDL initialization or real audio.

## Reproduction and preservation

From `/home/user/wine-assembly`:

```sh
node scratch/runs/20261020-midi-final-readonly-review/replay.js --mutations
REVIEW_PROBES=1 node scratch/runs/20261020-midi-final-readonly-review/replay.js
```

`replay.js` reads candidate source and repository dependencies from exact Git blobs into RAM, redirects mutation children to the same reader, and rejects filesystem write APIs. It uses the existing worktree only for module path resolution. `tests.log`, `probes.log`, and `verification.log` retain bounded results. Probes are diagnostic observations (exit 0), not assertions that the incorrect behavior conforms.

No checkout/setup/worktree creation/config writes/install/full build/runtime/source edits/main integration/worker/deployment occurred. Only this evidence directory and append-only board entries were written. No source commit required; coordinator preserves accepted review later. Existing evidence and laptop work preserved.
